findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext within the EC2 user_data script, which is visible to anyone with instance metadata access or console describe permissions, leading to credential leakage.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, meaning data at rest on the volume is unencrypted and vulnerable to exposure if the underlying storage is compromised.
The EBS snapshot inherits from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption configured, exposing potentially sensitive data at rest in the snapshot.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to brute-force and unauthorized access attempts from anywhere on the internet.
The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 with no other restriction, increasing attack surface for the web service exposed on this instance.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IP addresses and increasing exposure to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IP addresses and increasing exposure to the internet.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking exposure of sensitive network traffic logs.
